Summary.Title: First-Tier Triad Operationalization Scope Review
Summary.FirstTierDoctrine: IRLT, compounding pharmacy, and DSCSA remain equal first-tier commercialization and demonstration tracks.
Summary.HumanAuthorityRule: Qualified humans and authorized organizational roles retain binding authority.
Summary.SourceOfTruthRule: Official records and executed actions remain in governed source systems.
Summary.Step163Statement: Step 163 is a governed operationalization-scope review only. It does not authorize or implement Step 164.
Summary.Step164Gate: EXPLICIT HUMAN AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED AFTER STEP 163 REVIEW

Step164CandidateScope.ProposedTitle: First-Tier Triad Assurance Orchestrator and Evidence Passport API
Step164CandidateScope.Purpose: Implement one local synthetic orchestration layer over the Step 162 shared kernel that can launch controlled commercial demonstrations, expose read-only assurance state, generate evidence passports, issue RAMAT display feeds, inject governed failures, and export reconstruction packages for IRLT, compounding pharmacy, and DSCSA.
RequiredCapabilities: Strict JSON input and output schema
RequiredDemonstrations: IRLT time or custody failure and recovery
Compounding formula, label, or timing failure and recovery
DSCSA serialization, EPCIS, partner, or suspect-product failure and recovery
ExplicitExclusions: No real product transfer or shipment
Step164CandidateScope.AuthorizationReason: Step 164 requires a new explicit accountable-human authorization after Step 163 review.

SharedOperationalizationCapabilities.Purpose: Register IRLT, compounding pharmacy, and DSCSA scenarios through one governed schema.
Standardize identity, evidence, dependency, authority, timing, No-Bind, and admissibility inputs and outputs.
Expose synthetic evaluation, status, passport, display, and reconstruction endpoints without source-system writes.
Generate portable synthetic identity, provenance, integrity, dependency, authority, and decision packages.
Provide expiring, redacted, display-only assurance contracts for each first-tier track.
Deterministically introduce identity, integrity, dependency, authority, timing, and source-state failures.
Export chronology, evidence references, decisions, No-Bind events, human prompts, and unresolved gaps.
Run controlled baseline, failure, hold, recovery, and admissibility demonstrations for each track.
Generate repeatable tests, audit evidence, backup verification, and SHA-256 artifact integrity.
Ensure every admissible state still requires qualified human decision and governed source-system execution.

GovernanceGates.Requirement: An accountable human must explicitly authorize Step 164 after reviewing Step 163.
IRLT, compounding pharmacy, and DSCSA remain equal first-tier tracks.
Platform B v1 remains limited to its six frozen capabilities.
Shared advanced evaluation and operationalization logic belongs only to Platform B1 / MVP2.
Thread D2 and RAMAT Vision remain DISPLAY / WITNESS ONLY.
Any Step 164 local API must be synthetic and read-only with no production write-back.
Qualified humans and authorized organizational roles retain binding authority.
Official records and execution remain in governed source systems.
Step 164 may use synthetic records and mock identities only.
Missing, stale, conflicted, invalid, or compromised conditions must create or preserve a hold.
Evidence integrity, SHA-256 sealing, rehashing, and tamper detection remain mandatory.
Step 164 must include tests, audit evidence, backup or reset, recovery, and integrity verification.
No release, dispensing, administration, shipment, product transfer, or other regulated execution is authorized.

OperationalizationTracks.StrategicPosition: Equal first-tier commercialization and demonstration priority
OperationalizationTracks.OperationalPainPoint: A preparation may appear complete while prescription, patient, formula, ingredient, calculation, equipment, environmental, labeling, timing, or pharmacist dependencies disagree.
OperationalizationTracks.ProposedDemonstration: Synthetic prescription-to-dispensing readiness passport covering order identity, formula version, ingredient genealogy, calculations, preparation, labeling, beyond-use timing, pharmacist authority, and dispensing readiness.
OperationalizationTracks.RequiredKernelReuse: Identity; evidence sealing; rehash verification; dependency evaluation; authority evaluation; temporal validity; No-Bind; admissibility; RAMAT display contract; reconstruction
OperationalizationTracks.ProposedNewCapabilities: Formula dependency graph; ingredient genealogy; calculation verification; label comparison; beyond-use timing; pharmacist review passport
OperationalizationTracks.RequiredFailureProof: Order mismatch, wrong formula, unreleased ingredient, calculation conflict, label mismatch, expired beyond-use time, or missing pharmacist authority must create a hold.
OperationalizationTracks.RequiredSuccessProof: All synthetic prescription, formula, ingredient, calculation, label, timing, and pharmacist-authority conditions must be satisfied before ACTION ADMISSIBLE.
OperationalizationTracks.HumanAuthority: Authorized prescriber context, qualified compounding personnel, authorized pharmacist, and accountable pharmacy management
OperationalizationTracks.SourceSystemBoundary: Mock pharmacy, formulation, inventory, equipment, environmental, label, and dispensing systems remain authoritative.
OperationalizationTracks.RamatRole: DISPLAY / WITNESS ONLY for order identity, formula, ingredients, calculation, timing, label, authority, and No-Bind state
OperationalizationTracks.CommercialOutput: Compounding Assurance Passport, ingredient genealogy view, pharmacist readiness view, and defensible preparation reconstruction

OperationalizationTracks.StrategicPosition: Equal first-tier commercialization and demonstration priority
OperationalizationTracks.OperationalPainPoint: A serialized product may appear transferable while serial, lot, aggregation, EPCIS, transaction evidence, trading-partner authority, custody, or suspect-product state is unresolved.
OperationalizationTracks.ProposedDemonstration: Synthetic manufacturer-to-dispenser assurance passport covering serialization, EPCIS event sequence, aggregation, transaction evidence, trading-partner authority, custody, verification, suspect-product hold, and disposition readiness.
OperationalizationTracks.RequiredKernelReuse: Canonical identity; evidence sealing; rehash verification; source agreement; authority evaluation; No-Bind; admissibility; RAMAT display contract; reconstruction
OperationalizationTracks.ProposedNewCapabilities: Serial and lot graph; EPCIS event-chain verification; aggregation integrity; trading-partner passport; suspect-product workflow; transaction evidence passport
OperationalizationTracks.RequiredFailureProof: Serial mismatch, broken aggregation, missing EPCIS event, unauthorized trading partner, incomplete transaction evidence, or suspect-product state must create a governed hold.
OperationalizationTracks.RequiredSuccessProof: Serialization, EPCIS, aggregation, partner authority, transaction evidence, custody, and suspect-product clearance must be satisfied before ACTION ADMISSIBLE.
OperationalizationTracks.HumanAuthority: Authorized manufacturer, trading-partner, supply-chain, compliance, investigation, Quality, and disposition roles
OperationalizationTracks.SourceSystemBoundary: Mock serialization, EPCIS, ERP, warehouse, trading-partner, verification, and investigation systems remain authoritative.
OperationalizationTracks.RamatRole: DISPLAY / WITNESS ONLY for product identity, event-chain integrity, partner authority, suspect-product state, No-Bind, and transfer readiness
OperationalizationTracks.CommercialOutput: DSCSA Assurance Passport, chain-of-custody truth view, trading-partner passport, and suspect-product investigation reconstruction

OperationalizationTracks.StrategicPosition: Equal first-tier commercialization and demonstration priority
OperationalizationTracks.OperationalPainPoint: Time-critical radiopharmaceutical work can appear complete in one system while release, custody, timing, equipment, material, or receiving dependencies remain unresolved.
OperationalizationTracks.ProposedDemonstration: AURORA-17 batch-to-administration assurance passport covering manufacturing, QC, human release authority, decay window, custody transfer, transport, receipt, and administration readiness.
OperationalizationTracks.RequiredKernelReuse: Identity; SHA-256 sealing; rehash verification; dependency evaluation; authority evaluation; temporal validity; No-Bind; admissibility; RAMAT display contract; reconstruction
OperationalizationTracks.ProposedNewCapabilities: Time-to-expiry engine; custody event sequence; transport-condition evidence; receiving-site readiness; decay-window risk state; IRLT evidence passport
OperationalizationTracks.RequiredFailureProof: Expired decay window, custody gap, wrong receiving site, evidence mismatch, or unavailable release authority must create ACTION HELD and NO-BIND STATE ACTIVE.
OperationalizationTracks.RequiredSuccessProof: All evidence, timing, identity, custody, authority, and receiving dependencies must be positively satisfied before ACTION ADMISSIBLE.
OperationalizationTracks.HumanAuthority: Authorized batch releaser, Quality Unit, radiation-safety role, logistics custodian, receiving-site authority, and qualified clinical personnel
OperationalizationTracks.SourceSystemBoundary: Mock MES, LIMS, eQMS, ERP, custody, transport, and administration systems remain authoritative.
OperationalizationTracks.RamatRole: DISPLAY / WITNESS ONLY for timing, identity, evidence, custody, authority, No-Bind, and human-action prompts
OperationalizationTracks.CommercialOutput: IRLT Assurance Passport, live time-risk view, custody truth chain, and regulator-ready reconstruction package
